name: glastyn

attributes.attribute: a form of the spectral water horse
lived on the Isle of Man
recorded by MacKillop as a variant spelling of glashtin

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The glastyn, also spelled glashtin, is a Manx folkloric figure. This form of the spectral water horse dwelt on the Isle of Man. He appeared as a handsome man rather than a horse. MacKillop lists glastyn as a variant spelling of glashtin. He belongs to the wider family of Celtic water horses found across the islands. The creature forms part of the wider Celtic water-horse family that runs from the Manx glashtin to the Scottish kelpie and each-uisge. Folklore ties it to riverbanks, lake shores, and the strand.

okr.objective: Present the Manx water horse known as the glastyn and note MacKillop’s variant spelling link to glashtin.
